2022-07-30.basis: Cato’s fiscal Q2 2022 earnings release first established that consolidated GAAP total revenue met the threshold. For the quarter ended July 30, 2022, Cato reported $196,864,000 against $207,746,000 for the quarter ended July 31, 2021. The 95% cutoff was $197,358,700, so actual revenue was $494,700 below it. Both figures include retail sales and other revenue on the same consolidated basis.

coverage.detail: March 17, 2022, preceding earnings cycle. The fiscal Q4 2021 release compared historical sales with 2020 and 2019. Management discussed cost and consumer spending pressures through 2022 without quantifying fiscal Q2 2022 revenue.
May 19, 2022, fiscal Q1 release. The 3% sales decline applied to the quarter ended April 30. The CEO expressed caution about the rest of the year and gave no numeric Q2 revenue outlook.
The May annual-meeting 8-K reported voting results, a credit agreement and the Q1 earnings release. Its exhibit list contained no investor presentation or separate guidance update.
The fiscal Q1 10-Q anticipated collection of an income tax receivable by the end of Q2. It gave no numeric Q2 consolidated revenue forecast.

Cato’s issuer newswire history lists only the May 20 quarterly dividend announcement between the May 19 and August 18 earnings releases. Searches for interim preliminary results, updated guidance, investor presentations and dated public management remarks or calls found no earlier Q2 revenue bound.
August 18 actuals. The consolidated income statement reports Q2 sales of $195,006,000 plus other revenue of $1,858,000, totaling $196,864,000. The prior-year total on the same row was $207,746,000.
The 8-K explicitly confirms Cato issued the release on August 18 for the second quarter ended July 30. The 8-K was signed August 22.
The August 25 Form 10-Q confirms both quarterly total revenue figures already public on August 18.

2022-07-30.publication_date_evidence: Cato’s original wire release was published August 18, 2022 at 07:00 ET. The subsequent 8-K independently confirms that issue date. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cato-reports-2q-results-301608151.html

2023-04-29.basis: Cato’s fiscal Q1 2023 earnings release first established the decline. Its consolidated income statement reports total revenues of $192,050,000 for the quarter ended April 29, 2023, versus $206,721,000 for the quarter ended April 30, 2022. That was a 7.10% decline, below the $196,384,950 cutoff. Both totals include retail sales and other revenue.

coverage.detail: November 17, 2022, fiscal Q3 release. Management discussed inflation, inventory and markdowns. It gave no numeric fiscal Q1 2023 revenue outlook.

Cato’s wire archive lists dividend announcements on November 18 and February 24, the latter also covering share repurchases. The March 16 and May 18 earnings releases are consecutive entries. Searches for preliminary results, updated guidance, investor presentations, calls and dated management remarks found no earlier qualifying disclosure.

March 16, 2023, fiscal Q4 and full-year 2022 release. Management expected continued pressure on customer spending and quantified planned store openings and closures for 2023. It gave no Q1 consolidated revenue figure or range.

The fiscal 2022 annual report includes the March 23 Form 10-K and the CEO’s shareholder letter. The letter discusses cautious planning, inflation and interest rates for 2023 without quantifying Q1 revenue.
The April proxy materials gave no Q1 revenue outlook. They scheduled the annual meeting for May 18 at 11:30 a.m. Eastern, after the earnings release.

May 18 actuals. In thousands of dollars, the GAAP table gives retail sales of 190,311 plus other revenue of 1,739 for 2023, and 204,933 plus 1,788 for 2022. The total-revenue row supplies the requested comparison.
The May 22 Form 8-K confirms Cato issued the earnings release on May 18 and furnished it as Exhibit 99.1.
EDGAR records May 25 as the Form 10-Q filing date for the April 29 quarter, one week after the public release.

2023-04-29.publication_date_evidence: Cato’s investor-relations release is dated May 18, 2023. Its wire archive records distribution at 7:00 a.m. Eastern that day, and the subsequent Form 8-K independently confirms the issue date. https://catocorp.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cato-reports-1q-earnings-0

2022-07-02.basis: Tuesday Morning’s September 23 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure. Its consolidated statements of operations report Q4 FY2022 net sales of $161,934,000 for the three months ended July 2, 2022, against $177,274,000 for the three months ended June 30, 2021. The decline was 8.65%, below the $168,410,300 sales ceiling. Earlier quarterly forecasts covered comparable stores. The September 16 preliminary sales estimate covered the full year and supplied no quarterly upper bound.

coverage.detail: February 3 Q2 release. Management projected mid-single-digit comparable-store sales growth for Q3 and low- to mid-single-digit comparable-store sales growth for the second half. Neither forecast established Q4 consolidated sales.

May 12 Q3 release. Management forecast a 3% to 5% year-over-year decline in Q4 comparable-store sales. The high end was a 3% decline, and the measure covered comparable stores. The consolidated table reported nine-month net sales of $587,875,000.

May 12 public earnings call. Management discussed the March and April sales slowdown and its Q4 outlook. The call supplied no separate ceiling for consolidated Q4 net sales. The search for intervening presentations and public remarks identified no qualifying forecast.

July 29 outlook update. Management revised the expected Q4 comparable-store sales decline to 8%. The release gave no consolidated net-sales figure or reconciliation from comparable stores to all sales.
September 9 stockholder letter. Management described reduced traffic and sales while explaining its financing needs. It gave no quarterly sales amount or percentage decline.
September 9 financing announcement. The company scheduled its results for around September 23 and disclosed no Q4 consolidated sales figure.

September 16 Form 12b-25. Management estimated a full-year sales increase of approximately $59 million. Applying that estimate to FY2021 sales of $690.790 million and subtracting reported nine-month sales implies Q4 sales near $161.915 million. The annual estimate had no stated upper endpoint, and the filing’s Q4 commentary referred only to comparable stores.

September 21 financing close. The $35 million was convertible debt financing completed after quarter-end. The announcement supplied no Q4 sales figure or change to the reported quarter’s revenue perimeter.
September 23 actuals. The quarterly net-sales row reports 161,934 and 177,274 in thousands of dollars. Both values come directly from the issuer’s consolidated table.
The original wire release identifies Tuesday Morning Corp. as its source and records publication at 07:00 ET on September 23.

2022-07-02.publication_date_evidence: The SEC Exhibit 99.1 carries a Dallas dateline of September 23, 2022. The issuer’s GlobeNewswire distribution independently timestamps the same announcement at 07:00 ET that day, before the September 28 Form 10-K filing.

2022-09-01.basis: Micron’s June 30 earnings release gave FQ4-22 consolidated GAAP revenue guidance of $7.2 billion ± $400 million. The $7.6 billion high end was below $7.8603 billion, the threshold of 95% of FQ4-21 reported revenue of $8.274 billion.

coverage.detail: March 29, preceding earnings cycle. Micron guided FQ3-22 GAAP revenue to $8.7 billion ± $200 million. Its record-revenue outlook covered the full fiscal year and supplied no FQ4 revenue ceiling.
May 12 Investor Day. Micron presented a cross-cycle revenue growth target. The presentation supplied no FQ4-22 consolidated revenue ceiling.
June 30, FQ3 earnings release. The FQ4-22 Business Outlook table explicitly gave a GAAP revenue range of $6.8 billion to $7.6 billion. This was the first qualifying disclosure found.
June 30 earnings call. Management’s prepared remarks repeated the FQ4 revenue outlook. The same-day release independently established its GAAP basis.
August 9 interim update. Ahead of its CFO’s public KeyBanc webcast, Micron said FQ4 revenue could come in at or below the June 30 range’s $6.8 billion low end.

September 29 actual results. The consolidated statements of operations reported $6,643 million for the quarter ended September 1, 2022 and $8,274 million for the quarter ended September 2, 2021, a 19.71% decline.
EDGAR records acceptance of the June 30 Form 8-K at 16:00:27 that day and identifies Exhibit 99.1 as the earnings release.

2022-09-01.publication_date_evidence: Micron’s release is dated June 30, 2022. The SEC filing index independently confirms that the Form 8-K containing the release was accepted on June 30, 2022 at 16:00:27.

2022-06-30.basis: nLIGHT’s August 4 earnings release was the earliest verified qualifying disclosure. For the three months ended June 30, consolidated GAAP revenue fell from $69,113,000 in 2021 to $60,827,000 in 2022, a 12.0% decline. Both totals include product and development revenue. The May outlook’s $67,000,000 high end exceeded the $65,657,350 cutoff.

coverage.detail: February 17, preceding earnings cycle. The $61 million to $67 million revenue outlook applied only to Q1 2022. The release gave no Q2 revenue range.
May 5, Q1 earnings release. Management forecast Q2 revenue of $59 million to $67 million. The high end exceeded the cutoff by $1,342,650.
May 5 earnings-call presentation, slide 13. Management repeated the $59 million to $67 million range and explicitly identified $63 million as its midpoint.
The June investor presentation showed historical quarterly revenue through Q1 2022 and supplied no updated Q2 consolidated revenue ceiling.
The June annual-meeting 8-K reported shareholder voting results under Item 5.07 and supplied no Q2 revenue update.
The July 8-K addressed executive compensation under Item 5.02 and supplied no Q2 revenue update.
July 21. nLIGHT confirmed the June 30 quarter end and scheduled the results for August 4 after market close. The notice contained no preliminary revenue figure.
August 4, Exhibit 99.1. The consolidated statements report Q2 product revenue of $48,180,000 and development revenue of $12,647,000, totaling $60,827,000 against $69,113,000 a year earlier.
August 4 earnings-call presentation, slide 3. Management compared the actual total to the guidance it had issued in early May.
EDGAR records acceptance of the results 8-K and its earnings-release exhibit on August 4, 2022 at 16:08:03.

2022-06-30.publication_date_evidence: Exhibit 99.1 carries an August 4, 2022 dateline and says nLIGHT reported the results that day. The same-day EDGAR acceptance independently confirms public availability before the August 5 Form 10-Q.

2022-09-30.basis: Reed’s Q3 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its condensed statements of operations report company-wide GAAP net sales of $12,094,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2022, compared with $13,402,000 for the same quarter of 2021. Sales fell 9.76% year over year and were $637,900 below the $12,731,900 threshold. Both figures come from the same Net Sales row. The $3.8 million shipment delay discussed in the release shifted sales into Q4 and requires no adjustment to reported Q3 sales.

coverage.detail: May 16 Q1 release. Reed’s projected $59–62 million of fiscal 2022 net sales. Management described renewed growth in Q2 and gave no Q3 sales ceiling.
May 16 public call transcript. Management reiterated the annual sales range and discussed second-half growth initiatives without quantifying Q3 company-wide sales.
August 11 Q2 release. Reed’s maintained its $59–62 million full-year net sales outlook. Its explicit Q3 and Q4 forecast concerned positive cash flow. It gave no Q3 revenue range.

August 11 public call transcript. Management discussed Q3 and Q4 inventory and transportation costs. Its seasonal swing-lid forecast was in cases for the year. None of those figures bounded total Q3 net sales.
September investor presentation. The revenue chart labels its forecast 2022F and attributes it to August 11 guidance. The presentation gives no Q3 company-wide sales ceiling.

September 21 Form 8-K addressed broker voting on an annual-meeting proposal. The August 22 and August 24 current reports concerned Nasdaq delisting proceedings and Reed’s appeal. These disclosures supplied no Q3 sales figure.
October 3 release announced a Nasdaq listing extension and compliance milestones. Its financial thresholds concerned share price and stockholders’ equity.
October 6 Form 8-K reported the October 5 shareholder votes and Nasdaq deadlines, with no Q3 sales update.
October 26 issuer announcement scheduled the November 10 call and said a results release would precede it. It disclosed no preliminary sales.
October 31 Form S-1. The offering materials use June 30 financial information and give no preliminary September-quarter sales or Q3 sales ceiling.
November 10 Form 8-K, Item 2.02, confirms Reed’s issued the Q3 results release that day and attached it as Exhibit 99.1.
The November 14 Form 10-Q confirms the release’s quarterly GAAP net sales of $12,094,000 and $13,402,000.
The original issuer-distributed release identifies Reed’s as the source and records publication at 4:05 p.m. ET on November 10, before the 5:00 p.m. call.

2022-09-30.publication_date_evidence: The original Reed’s wire release is timestamped November 10, 2022 at 16:05 ET. Item 2.02 of its Form 8-K independently confirms that Reed’s issued Exhibit 99.1 on November 10.

2023-03-31.basis: Reed’s June 1 earnings release was the earliest qualifying communication found. Its GAAP statement of operations reported net sales of $11,157,000 for the three months ended March 31, 2023, against $12,182,000 for the same quarter of 2022. That was an 8.41% decline and $415,900 below the $11,572,900 threshold. Both figures come from the same company-wide net sales row.

coverage.detail: November 10, 2022, preceding earnings cycle. The $56 million to $59 million sales range covered FY 2022. Management’s 2023 targets concerned modified EBITDA and cash flow. Neither supplied a Q1 2023 sales bound.
February 1 preliminary release. The $15.1 million revenue estimate covered Q4 2022. Reed’s projected double-digit net revenue growth for full-year 2023 without quantifying Q1 sales.

March 29, previous earnings release and call. Reed’s reiterated double-digit full-year 2023 revenue growth. Its Q1 remarks described distribution gains. The call’s reference to a significant first-quarter decrease concerned borrowing costs. No qualifying Q1 sales forecast was identified in the release or call remarks.
April 3 issuer announcement. The Roundy’s agreement expanded retail distribution without quantifying company-wide Q1 sales.

May 15 annual report. The financial statements covered the year ended December 31, 2022. March 31, 2023 disclosures included share counts and the interim CFO appointment. No Q1 sales amount or range was identified.

May 16 late-filing notice for Q1. Reed’s cited the time needed for auditor review and checked No in Part IV(3) on an anticipated significant change in operating results. It supplied no sales estimate.
The May 22 issuer notice, reproduced here, scheduled the results call for June 1 and said Reed’s would release results before the call. It gave no sales figure.

May 31 Form 8-K and financing announcement. The $5.6 million comprised a $4.1 million equity investment and $1.5 million in additional bridge financing. The announcement supplied no Q1 sales figure. The intervening search found no qualifying preliminary result, investor presentation or public management update.
June 1 earnings release furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The statement of operations gives Q1 2023 and Q1 2022 net sales of 11,157 and 12,182, respectively, in thousands of dollars.

2023-03-31.publication_date_evidence: Reed’s investor-relations page displays June 1, 2023 as the release date. The SEC-filed copy of the same earnings announcement carries a June 1, 2023 Norwalk dateline.

2022-12-31.basis: Matson’s February 21 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its consolidated income statement reports total operating revenue of $801.6 million for Q4 2022 and $1,267.0 million for Q4 2021, a 36.73% decline. The 95% threshold was $1,203.65 million. Both columns include Ocean Transportation and Logistics as reported, including the effect of ending the temporary CCX service.

coverage.detail: July 19 preliminary Q2 release. Management expected vessels to operate near capacity for the remainder of 2022 and freight rates to command a premium. Its numeric earnings ranges applied to Q2. It gave no Q4 consolidated revenue ceiling.
August 1 Q2 earnings release. The $1,261.1 million consolidated revenue figure was a Q2 actual. Management discussed freight demand and rates without quantifying Q4 consolidated revenue.
August 1 Q2 call slides. The outlook covered domestic trade and Transpacific market conditions. The $160 million to $180 million forecast was full-year capital expenditure.

October 17 preliminary Q3 release. After ending CCX in September, management expected lower year-over-year freight demand and rates for its CLX and CLX+ services through year-end. It gave no numerical Q4 consolidated revenue forecast.

November 2 Q3 earnings release. Consolidated revenue of $1,114.8 million applied to the quarter ended September 30. The forward outlook described weaker freight demand and rates without setting a Q4 revenue ceiling.

November 2 management call presentation, slide 4. Management expected challenging Transpacific conditions for the next two quarters. Its forecast concerned demand and rates on two China services and gave no company-wide revenue range.

January 18 preliminary Q4 release. Matson estimated Ocean Transportation operating income at $70–80 million, Logistics operating income at $12–13 million and net income at $69.9–74.8 million. The 47.2% decline measured China container volume. None of these figures established consolidated revenue.
January 18 preliminary earnings supplement, slide 4. The income statement estimates began with operating income of $82–93 million. The supplement supplied no total revenue estimate.

February 21 actual results, consolidated income statement, page 8. In the three-month columns, Ocean Transportation revenue of $633.0 million plus Logistics revenue of $168.6 million totaled $801.6 million. The corresponding prior-year total was $1,267.0 million.
The SEC filing index identifies the earnings release as Exhibit 99.1 and records acceptance of the Form 8-K on February 21, 2023 at 16:05:40.

2022-12-31.publication_date_evidence: Matson’s release carries a Honolulu dateline of February 21, 2023 and announces the quarterly results that day. EDGAR independently records same-day publication of the release as Exhibit 99.1.

2023-03-31.basis: The May 3 issuer earnings table reports actual Q1 consolidated net sales of $5,103.1 million against $5,949.1 million, down 14.2%. The April 18 CFO statement quantified preliminary results only as approximately $5.1 billion without an exact figure or a bounded interval.

coverage.detail: November 2, 2022, preceding earnings cycle. CDW’s quarterly outlook covered sequential average daily sales for Q4 2022. Its full-year sales outlook used a combined, constant-currency basis. Neither supplied a Q1 2023 reported sales ceiling.

November 29 Credit Suisse conference. CDW’s event page confirms the date. The conference opened with a statement that forward-looking remarks were dated as of the November 2 earnings release. [Conference transcript opening](https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/CDW/transcripts/2160152)
February 8, 2023. The Q4 release reported $5,438.3 million of consolidated net sales over 63 selling days, the base for management’s sequential Q1 outlook.

February 8 earnings presentation, slide 25. CDW projected flat to low-single-digit sequential growth in average daily sales. With 64 Q1 selling days, the threshold allowed at most 2.2992% daily sales growth. A 3% increase would yield $5,690.4 million ($5,438.3 million × 64/63 × 1.03), above the threshold. CDW gave no tighter numerical cap.

March 7 Morgan Stanley conference. CFO Albert Miralles discussed a roughly flat 2023 IT market, expected CDW outperformance of 200–300 basis points, and first-half spending patterns. His remarks supplied no numerical Q1 consolidated sales ceiling. [Transcript of the CFO’s remarks](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/cdw/transcripts/56697-morgan-stanley-technology-media-telecom-conference/)

April 18 preliminary results. The CFO stated, “First quarter Net sales were approximately $5.1 billion.” CDW gave one preliminary dollar estimate. Its separate full-year industry and constant-currency outlook did not enter the comparison.

May 3 actual results. CDW Corporation and subsidiaries reported consolidated net sales of $5,103.1 million against $5,949.1 million for the three months ended March 31, a reported decline of 14.2%. The release gives both periods on the same reported basis.

Checked the period between the company’s April 18 preannouncement and May 3 results. The 8-K inventory has no intervening current reports, and the company identified May 3 as its quarterly earnings call.

2023-03-31.publication_date_evidence: The CDW results release and public investor call are dated May 3, 2023.

indicative_earlier_disclosure.qualification: Approximately $5.1 billion. No explicit bound on the estimate; excluded from the exact-figure/wholly qualifying range date.

2023-06-30.basis: Black Knight’s August 3 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its consolidated statements of earnings show revenue of $368.2 million for the three months ended June 30, 2023, versus $394.5 million a year earlier. The reported decline was 6.67%, and revenue was $6.575 million below the $374.775 million cutoff. The release separately deducts $10.0 million of prior-year TitlePoint revenue to calculate organic growth. The reported GAAP comparison retains that revenue in the $394.5 million base.

coverage.detail: February 28, Q4 and full-year 2022 release. Black Knight said it had suspended forward guidance during the proposed ICE acquisition and would hold no earnings call. It supplied no Q2 2023 revenue range.
May 4, Q1 2023 release. The $382.2 million revenue figure covered the March quarter. The Business Outlook section confirmed guidance remained suspended and there would be no Q1 earnings call.
The May 4 investor presentation reported Q1 results and historical comparisons. It gave no upper bound for Q2 consolidated revenue.
The 8-K covering the July 12 annual meeting reported shareholder votes and contained no Q2 revenue update.

July 17, Optimal Blue divestiture announcement. The $700 million figure was the purchase price for a sale contingent on completion of the ICE merger. The announcement gave no Q2 consolidated revenue figure.

July 20, Q2 reporting notice. Black Knight scheduled results for August 3 and reiterated that it would provide no forward guidance or earnings call. The notice contained no preliminary results. The intervening search found no dated management remarks, presentation or guidance update that set a qualifying Q2 revenue bound.

August 3, Q2 results, Exhibit 99.1. The quarterly GAAP revenue row gives $368.2 million and $394.5 million. The separate organic reconciliation gives an adjusted prior-year base of $384.5 million and a 4% organic decline.
Black Knight’s own wire release identifies the issuer as the news provider and records public distribution at 7:30 a.m. ET on August 3.

2023-06-30.publication_date_evidence: Exhibit 99.1 is datelined August 3, 2023. Black Knight’s wire distribution independently timestamps the same results at 7:30 a.m. ET that day.

2023-07-01.basis: Silicon Labs’ April 26 earnings release forecast consolidated fiscal Q2 2023 revenue of $238 million to $248 million. The high end was $1,992,500 below the cutoff of $249,992,500, calculated as 95% of reported fiscal Q2 2022 revenue of $263,150,000. The release gave one company-wide revenue range and applied its GAAP and non-GAAP distinctions to other measures.

coverage.detail: February 1, 2023, preceding earnings cycle. The $242 million to $252 million revenue outlook covered fiscal Q1, the three months ending April 1. The release gave no Q2 revenue range.
On the February 1 earnings call, CFO John Hollister expressly assigned the $242 million to $252 million range to Q1. The call supplied no numeric Q2 ceiling.
Silicon Labs announced a public March 8 fireside chat with its CEO and CFO. The announcement contained no revenue forecast.
Management’s March 8 remarks discussed design wins and the years over which those wins generate revenue. They supplied no numeric consolidated revenue ceiling for fiscal Q2 2023.
April 26, Form 8-K Exhibit 99, Business Outlook. Silicon Labs stated, “The company expects second-quarter revenue to be between $238 to $248 million.” The entire range qualified.
The May 24 notice announced presentations at TD Cowen on June 1 and Stifel on June 6. Both events followed the qualifying April outlook. The notice gave no updated revenue range.

The issuer’s release archive between April 26 and July 26 lists conference, product and lab announcements. The July 13 earnings webcast notice announced the results date. No preliminary Q2 sales release appeared in that interval.

July 26 actuals confirmed the decline. The same condensed consolidated income statement reports revenue of $244,866,000 for the three months ended July 1, 2023 and $263,150,000 for the three months ended July 2, 2022.

2023-07-01.publication_date_evidence: Form 8-K Item 2.02 explicitly says Silicon Laboratories issued the release on April 26, 2023. Exhibit 99 carries the same April 26 Austin dateline and contains the qualifying forecast.

2023-09-30.basis: Enphase’s July 27 Q2 earnings release gave a companywide Q3 2023 revenue outlook of $550 million to $600 million. Q3 2022 consolidated net revenue was $634,713,000, making the 95% cutoff $602,977,350. The forecast high end cleared the cutoff by $2,977,350, so the entire range qualified.

coverage.detail: The original Q3 2022 consolidated statement of operations reported net revenue of $634,713,000. Enphase carried the same amount as the prior-year comparator in its Q3 2023 results.

April 25, 2023. The preceding earnings cycle gave a $700 million to $750 million revenue range for Q2 2023. Management’s Q3 comments on the call concerned manufacturing, product introductions and IQ8 mix. The earlier disclosure search found no Q3 consolidated revenue ceiling.

May 17, 2023. Enphase’s annual-meeting archive includes the CEO letter and shareholder presentation. The search of meeting materials and dated management remarks found no qualifying Q3 revenue forecast.
July 12, 2023. Enphase scheduled the July 27 earnings call. The notice contained no Q3 revenue figure.

July 27, 2023. Under the Q3 2023 financial outlook, Enphase gave one revenue range covering GAAP results, $550 million to $600 million. The separately stated battery shipment estimate was an operating assumption within that revenue outlook.
EDGAR identifies Exhibit 99.1 as the Q2 earnings release and records acceptance of the Form 8-K on July 27 at 16:10:22 Eastern.

October 10, 2023. Enphase scheduled the October 26 results announcement without giving preliminary revenue. The search between the July release and October actuals found no separate preliminary or revised consolidated Q3 revenue range.

October 26, 2023. The consolidated statement of operations reported net revenue of $551,082,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2023, against $634,713,000 for the same three months of 2022. Actual revenue fell within the July range.

2023-09-30.publication_date_evidence: The issuer’s release carries a July 27, 2023 dateline. Item 2.02 of Enphase’s Form 8-K confirms that Enphase issued the release that day, and EDGAR recorded it before the scheduled 4:30 p.m. Eastern earnings call.

2023-09-30.basis: JetBlue’s October 31 earnings release first established the decline unambiguously. For the three months ended September 30, consolidated GAAP total operating revenues were $2,353 million in 2023 versus $2,562 million in 2022, down 8.2%. The 95% threshold was $2,433.9 million. August guidance allowed a decline as small as 4%, and the September update supplied no revised numeric upper bound.

coverage.detail: April 25 Q1 release. The revenue outlook covered Q2 growth of 4.5% to 8.5% and full-year growth of high single digits to low double digits. It gave no Q3 revenue range.
August 1 Q2 release. Estimated Q3 revenue growth ranged from −8% to −4% year over year. The −4% high end implied $2,459.52 million, above the $2,433.9 million threshold.
August 1 investor update explicitly identified the forecast quarter as ending September 30, 2023 and repeated the −8% to −4% revenue range.
The August 1 earnings presentation and management’s remarks on the Q2 call used the same Q3 revenue range.

September 28 operational update. JetBlue expected Q3 revenue to be “near the low end” of its previous range. The −8% figure was the prior low endpoint. Management supplied no point forecast or new numeric ceiling.
October 13 Form 8-K concerned a prepayment to Spirit shareholders under the pending merger agreement. Spirit remained outside JetBlue’s reported revenue base.
October 17 issuer announcement scheduled the Q3 results call for October 31 and supplied no preliminary revenue figure.
October 20 Form 8-K disclosed a credit agreement amendment and supplied no Q3 revenue estimate.
EDGAR lists the Q3 earnings release as Exhibit 99.1 and records acceptance of the results 8-K on October 31 at 06:30:29.

2023-09-30.publication_date_evidence: JetBlue dated Exhibit 99.1 October 31, 2023 and stated that it reported Q3 results that day. The same-day EDGAR acceptance independently confirms public availability before the 10:00 a.m. Eastern earnings call.

2023-09-30.basis: Spirit’s September 12 investor update lowered Q3 2023 total revenue guidance to $1,245,000,000–$1,255,000,000. The high end was $21,020,050 below the cutoff of $1,276,020,050, which equals 95% of Spirit’s Q3 2022 consolidated operating revenue of $1,343,179,000. The guidance covered Spirit’s company-wide revenue on the same basis as the reported quarterly comparison.

coverage.detail: April 26, Q1 earnings cycle. Spirit forecast $1.46–$1.48 billion of total revenue specifically for Q2. Its full-year guidance covered capital spending and capacity. It gave no Q3 revenue range.
July 24, Form 8-K. Spirit announced the August 3 earnings release and public call schedule without giving a Q3 revenue estimate.
August 3, Q2 earnings release. Management described weaker summer fares and forecast a Q3 operating margin between negative 5.5% and negative 7.5%. Those percentages measured margin.
August 3, accompanying investor update. Spirit forecast Q3 total revenue of $1.30–$1.32 billion and repeated that range on its earnings call. Even the low end exceeded the cutoff.

September 12, revised investor update. Spirit placed its new $1,245–$1,255 million Q3 total revenue range alongside its previous $1,300–$1,320 million range. Searches of intervening filings, investor presentations and public management remarks identified no earlier qualifying revision.
Item 7.01 confirms that Spirit provided the revised guidance to investors on September 12. EDGAR received the Form 8-K on September 13.

October 26, Q3 earnings release. For the three months ended September 30, Spirit’s consolidated statement of operations reported passenger plus other operating revenue of $1,258,543,000 in 2023 and $1,343,179,000 in 2022, a 6.3% decline.

2023-09-30.publication_date_evidence: Spirit’s Regulation FD disclosure explicitly says it provided the Q3 guidance update to investors on September 12, 2023. Exhibit 99.1 bears the same date.
